passage.title: Ants could hold the secret to a longer life

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text for Ants. The passage covers Ysabel Giraldo's research on Pheidole dentata ants: she studied four age groups, analysing behaviour (care of young, locating food via scent trails, effect of light, aggression when attacking prey) and brain health (number of dying cells, synaptic complexes where neurons meet in mushroom bodies, levels of two proteins associated with ageing). Giraldo was the first to use precise age data. The ants didn't behave as expected — they remained active despite old age.]

passage.title: What we know about marine debris

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text for marine debris. The passage discusses Chelsea Rochman's research reviewing studies on marine debris (ocean trash). Rochman was not the first researcher in this area. The main threats identified were small plastic pieces. Little research covers chemical contamination. Most studies focused on individual animals rather than populations. Lab concentrations of plastic didn't always match ocean levels. Rochman's work covers different types of danger, and most studies she reviewed were well designed. One study expected to find mussels harmed by plastic. Mussels don't choose plastic over natural diet. Future disasters such as oil spills are a concern.]
